subject.title: Feature: groupScope option to consolidate group sessions into main

question: Should trusted group or channel bindings be allowed to join the main session, and should that capability be per-binding only or also available as a global session default?
rationale: Joining main changes transcript visibility, queue serialization, outbound routing, and the documented non-main sandbox/tool boundary, so permanent configuration semantics require maintainer intent.

options.title: Per-binding opt-in only
options.body: Allow an explicitly matched trusted binding to route to main while preserving isolated behavior everywhere else and omitting a global collapse switch.

options.title: Global plus binding overrides
options.body: Accept the linked PR’s broader model after documenting the security implications and proving global defaults, override precedence, and upgrades.

options.title: Keep groups isolated
options.body: Reject group-to-main routing and use cross-session history, search, memory, or the broader shared-session design instead.

recommendation.title: Per-binding opt-in only
recommendation.body: Allow an explicitly matched trusted binding to route to main while preserving isolated behavior everywhere else and omitting a global collapse switch.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal spans session-key routing, route resolution, and the user-facing session and group security documentation.
